- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, model frequently overestimates future gains; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent peak to avoid inflationary bias.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show price divergence from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is flat or mildly trending, model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values to reduce false momentum signals.
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to underestimate price volatility; add 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
